info.title: winche
info.description: The winche command-line tool: set up and use a Winche Server from the terminal, test access rules locally, and deploy rules, indexes, settings and functions. Install with: dotnet tool install -g Winche.Cli

commands.name: apps
commands.description: The project's registered apps

commands.name: apps:create
commands.description:
Register an app (--id, --sdk flutter, --android-package, --apple-bundle-id,
--web-origin, comma-separated); then winche configure --app <id>

commands.name: apps:delete
commands.description:
Remove a registered app
projects:archive | projects:restore | projects:delete <id>
Archive a project (refused until restored), or delete an archived one for good
secrets, secrets:set smtp-password | keycloak-sync --provider <name>
The project's sign-in secrets (the value from WINCHE_SECRET, or typed unseen)
webhooks:secret <id> A webhook's signing secret (--rotate: a new one)
users, users:disable | users:enable | users:sign-out <email or uid>
Your apps' users (--search, --limit)

commands.name: configure
commands.description:
Write lib/winche_options.dart for a Flutter or Dart app, from a Winche server
(--url; default the emulators)
functions init [<dir>]
Make a functions folder (default functions/): an example, deno.json, types for VS Code
functions deploy [<dir>]
Deploy the functions folder through the console, as you (winche login) or a CI token

commands.name: data:move
commands.description: Where the project's database is; --db-name/--db-host/… moves it; --finish [--keep-old]

commands.name: start
commands.description:
Run the database, storage, auth and functions locally (Postgres in Docker; rules and functions reloaded on save)
emulators exec <cmd> Start the emulators, run <cmd> against them (e.g. your tests), stop, exit with its code
emulators token <uid> [claim=value …]
Print a sign-in token the emulators accept
emulators idtoken <google|apple> <email>
Print a fake Google or Apple ID token for the emulators' /auth/v1/signIn/idp

options.name: --console
options.description: Console URL, e.g. https://api.example.com/_console (or WINCHE_CONSOLE, or winche.json)

options.name: --project
options.description: a project id on the same Winche Server; configure: the project at --url/p/<id>

options.name: --token
options.description: A CI token (winche tokens:create, or Project settings → CI tokens) instead of a saved sign-in (or WINCHE_TOKEN)

options.name: --config
options.description: winche.json to use (default: the nearest one upward)

options.name: --only
options.description: database, storage, or database,storage (default: every file in winche.json)

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what deploy would change, without saving

options.name: --force
options.description: Deploy even when the console already has these rules

options.name: --skip-tests
options.description: Deploy without running the tests first

options.name: --yes
options.description: Don't ask before a rollback

options.name: --stdout
options.description: Print pulled rules instead of writing the files (pull)

options.name: --port
options.description: Loopback port for the sign-in callback (login; default 9005), or the emulators' port (9090)

options.name: --host
options.description: Emulators: the address to listen on (default localhost; 0.0.0.0 for devices)

options.name: --pg
options.description: Emulators: use this Postgres instead of a temporary one in Docker

options.name: --data
options.description: Emulators: keep stored files here (default: a temporary folder)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Emulators: don't print each request

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Emulators: show the servers' own logs

options.name: --out
options.description: configure: where to write (default lib/winche_options.dart)

options.name: --platforms
options.description: configure: android,ios,macos,web,windows,linux (default: the app's platform folders)

options.name: --app
options.description: configure: the app's id, from the console's Project settings → Your apps

options.name: --help
options.description: Show this help

options.name: --version
options.description: Show the version

options.name: --no-browser
options.description:
login:add            Sign in another account on the server, beside the one in use
login:list           The accounts signed in, by server (* is the one in use)
login:use <email>    Use that signed-in account on the server
logout [<email>]     End that account's sign-in on the server (none named: all of them)
2fa enable           Turn on two-step sign-in for your account (an authenticator app)
rules validate       Check the rules files (offline)
rules test           Run the allow/deny cases in the test files (offline)
rules deploy         Run the tests, then publish the rules files as new versions on the console
rules history [<v>]  List the console's rule versions, or show version <v> against the active one
rules rollback <v>   Make version <v> active again (saved as a new version)
rules diff           Show how the rules files differ from what the console enforces
rules pull           Write the console's live rules into the rules files

options.name: --yes
options.description: Don't ask before a rollback

options.name: --stdout
options.description: Print pulled rules instead of writing the files (pull)

options.name: --port
options.description: Loopback port for the sign-in callback (login; default 9005), or the emulators' port (9090)

options.name: --host
options.description: Emulators: the address to listen on (default localhost; 0.0.0.0 for devices)

options.name: --pg
options.description: Emulators: use this Postgres instead of a temporary one in Docker

options.name: --data
options.description: Emulators: keep stored files here (default: a temporary folder)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Emulators: don't print each request

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Emulators: show the servers' own logs

options.name: --out
options.description: configure: where to write (default lib/winche_options.dart)

options.name: --platforms
options.description: configure: android,ios,macos,web,windows,linux (default: the app's platform folders)

options.name: --console
options.description: Console URL, e.g. https://api.example.com/_console (or WINCHE_CONSOLE, or winche.json)

options.name: --project
options.description: a project id on the same Winche Server; configure: the project at --url/p/<id>

options.name: --token
options.description: A CI token (winche tokens:create, or Project settings → CI tokens) instead of a saved sign-in (or WINCHE_TOKEN)

options.name: --config
options.description: winche.json to use (default: the nearest one upward)

options.name: --only
options.description: database, storage, or database,storage (default: every file in winche.json)

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what deploy would change, without saving

options.name: --force
options.description: Deploy even when the console already has these rules

options.name: --skip-tests
options.description: Deploy without running the tests first

options.name: --yes
options.description: Don't ask before a rollback

options.name: --stdout
options.description: Print pulled rules instead of writing the files (pull)

options.name: --port
options.description: Loopback port for the sign-in callback (login; default 9005), or the emulators' port (9090)

options.name: --host
options.description: Emulators: the address to listen on (default localhost; 0.0.0.0 for devices)

options.name: --pg
options.description: Emulators: use this Postgres instead of a temporary one in Docker

options.name: --data
options.description: Emulators: keep stored files here (default: a temporary folder)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Emulators: don't print each request

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Emulators: show the servers' own logs

options.name: --out
options.description: configure: where to write (default lib/winche_options.dart)

options.name: --platforms
options.description: configure: android,ios,macos,web,windows,linux (default: the app's platform folders)

options.name: --app
options.description: configure: the app's id, from the console's Project settings → Your apps

options.name: --help
options.description: Show this help

options.name: --version
options.description: Show the version

options.name: --no-browser
options.description:
login:add            Sign in another account on the server, beside the one in use
login:list           The accounts signed in, by server (* is the one in use)
login:use <email>    Use that signed-in account on the server
logout [<email>]     End that account's sign-in on the server (none named: all of them)
2fa enable           Turn on two-step sign-in for your account (an authenticator app)
rules validate       Check the rules files (offline)
rules test           Run the allow/deny cases in the test files (offline)
rules deploy         Run the tests, then publish the rules files as new versions on the console
rules history [<v>]  List the console's rule versions, or show version <v> against the active one
rules rollback <v>   Make version <v> active again (saved as a new version)
rules diff           Show how the rules files differ from what the console enforces
rules pull           Write the console's live rules into the rules files
